title: Complaint of TE Larry Ball vs. Westminster Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue answered no; complaint denied; no specification sustained. Adopted 17 concur, 1 dissent, 1 recused, 5 absent.
first_summary: A complaint challenged Westminster Presbytery's denial of a challenge to its May 15, 2001 withdrawal plan. The SJC held that the Presbytery did not err because BCO 25 and the BCO Preface give a presbytery a right to withdraw and it did not act for local churches. The complaint was denied; the SJC did not sustain the specifications.
summary: A complaint challenged Westminster Presbytery's denial of a challenge to its May 15, 2001 plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC answered no: the Presbytery did not err, and denied the complaint. BCO 25's local-church withdrawal right and the BCO Preface's grassroots principles extend to presbyteries unless expressly excluded, so a presbytery may determine its own membership and affiliation. The plan did not 'act for' local churches; they retained rights to remain in the PCA or leave, and retained property and internal operations.
